## What this is

AMLab (Arduino Measurements Lab) is courseware for undergraduate and
postgraduate laboratory work in measurement science and technology, built on
the [ArduinoDriver](https://github.com/pbosetti/ArduinoDriver) platform.

## Authors

Paolo Bosetti, Department of Industrial Engineering, University of Trento.

ArduinoDriver, the `UsbIo` firmware and the Python and R bindings are by the
same author.

## How to contribute

Corrections, new experiments and measured reference data are welcome.

1. Every experiment lives in one folder under `experiments/` and follows the
   structure of [`experiments/_template/`](https://github.com/pbosetti/ArduinoMeasurementsLab/tree/main/experiments/_template);
   `tools/new-experiment.sh` copies it and fills in the identifiers.
2. Theory is written once in `_theory.qmd` and included by both the slides and
   the handbook; the same holds for `_procedure.qmd` and `_instructor.qmd`.
3. Analysis templates come in pairs — Python and R — with the same section
   headings, the same figure labels and the same output tables. Continuous
   integration renders both against the shipped reference data and fails if
   either fails.
4. All equations are LaTeX (`$...$`, `$$...$$`), never Unicode glyphs.
5. No invented numbers. Where a value depends on hardware that has not been
   measured yet, leave a visible `TODO (Paolo)` marker.

## Instructor edition

Instructor material — expected results, pitfalls, session timing and
assessment rubrics — lives in the same sources, inside blocks that are visible
only under the `instructor` profile:

```bash
quarto render --profile instructor    # output in _site-instructor/
```

That build is produced as a continuous-integration artifact and is **not**
deployed to the public site.

## Acknowledgements

The measurement-uncertainty treatment throughout follows the *Guide to the
Expression of Uncertainty in Measurement* [@gum2008]; the ADC characterization
experiments follow IEEE Std 1057 [@ieee1057] and IEEE Std 1241 [@ieee1241].
